data.title: Global brands shift hundreds of millions in orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
data.description:
Key points:
  • Zara, H&M, M&S, Celio shift Bangladesh orders, mostly to India
  • Brands divert $254 million in orders as factories shut
  • Bangladesh unrest causes over $400 million in production losses
  • Rising wages, energy shortages erode Bangladesh's cost edge
  • Temporary order shifts risk becoming long-term sourcing moves

By Ruma Paul

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country's competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, in a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh's economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second-largest apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.

VIETNAM, CAMBODIA AND INDONESIA ALSO BENEFIT

India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversions, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.

Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, though the rise was the smallest in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" and that he hoped all garment workers would resume work from Saturday.

Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global apparel industry standards.

The factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.

Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S , H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

Indian textile shares rallied after the Reuters report, with Gokaldas Exports jumping as much as 11% and Trident gaining about 5%. Other potential beneficiaries, including Welspun Living , KPR Mill and Vardhman Textiles rose around 2% each.

M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers.

"The wage increase has added to costs at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying," he said.

Mahmud Hasan Khan, the group's president, declined to name the brands but said temporarily shifting some orders elsewhere helps the industry retain global clients while minimising financial losses.

MORE BUSINESS AT RISK

Factory owners said the bigger concern was that orders already diverted could be followed by the loss of future business as buyers reassessed where to source garments.

Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power sources.

Chowdhury said buyers were increasingly prioritising delivery times over price when choosing suppliers.

"Price becomes secondary when brands are under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines," he said.

India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.

Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.

The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery commitments.

Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business.

"Since November 1, most of my buyers have stopped placing orders because of the unrest," Alam said. "They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions."

Political tensions surrounding former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's possible return to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption.

Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved.

"The challenge is restoring buyers' confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions," he said. "Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists."

Headquarters: 9 Grigore Alexandrescu Street, 1st District, Bucharest, Romania

Phone no.: 004-021-2085035

Subscribed and paid in share capital: RON 3,395,530,040

Regulated market where the issued securities are traded: Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB: EL and EL30E), London Stock Exchange (LSE - ELSA and 51FL) and Luxembourg Stock Exchange (LuxSE - XS3111004241)

Significant events to be reported: Signing of a EUR 500,000,000 Bridge Facility Agreement

Electrica informs its shareholders and investors that on 26 November 2026 it signed, as borrower, a bridge facility agreement (the "Facility Agreement") for up to EUR 500,000,000, with Erste Group Bank AG, acting as Bookrunner and Mandated Lead Arranger, Documentation Agent and Original Lender, Banca Transilvania S.A. and ING Bank N.V. Amsterdam, Bucharest Branch as Original Lenders and Banca Comercială Română S.A. as Agent.

The Facility Agreement was concluded under Resolution no. 1/2026 of Electrica's Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders („EGMS”) of 29 April 2026. The resolution approved "the contracting by Societatea Energetică Electrica S.A. of one or more secured / unsecured loans in a total amount of up to EUR 1,000,000,000 (of a "bridge" type compared to the bonds to be issued by the Company), based on a credit agreement/credit agreements (generically referred to as the "Credit Agreement") concluded with one or more financial institutions (the "Financing Parties"), having a repayment term of up to maximum 24 months from the disbursement date of each relevant loan.". More details can be found in the Resolution available here, items 20 and 21.

The facility serves as bridge financing ahead of the bonds to be issued under the EUR 1,000,000,000 Euro Medium Term Note Programme („EMTN Programme”). The EMTN Programme was approved by the EGMS through the same Resolution of 29 April 2026 (items 18 and 19).  Its base prospectus was approved by the Luxembourg Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier on 29 October 2026. More details about the EMTN can be found here.

The amounts borrowed under the Facility Agreement are for financing Electrica’s general corporate purposes in respect of which proceeds are permitted to be applied in accordance with the EMTN Programme, excluding the payment of dividends.

Statement by Mr. Alexandru Chirita, CEO: "To our partners Erste Group Bank, Banca Transilvania, ING Bank, and Banca Comercială Romanian, as well to our colleagues at Electrica, who took the transaction from shareholder approval to signing, I extend my appreciation – thank you! We arrived here step by step: In April 2026, shareholders approved the bond Programme and the bridge financing. In September, Fitch reconfirmed the BBB- rating, with a stable outlook. In October, the base prospectus of the EMTN Programme was approved and the program was established.

Optimizing and reducing costs, as well as ensuring liquidity in advance for investment projects, are part of our management strategy. We will continue as follows: financing contracted in advance, at the lowest possible costs, for a company that invests in networks, production, and storage, but especially in people, while also bringing added value to its investors."
